source_review.notes: Checked ISO's current OSI Basic Reference Model record, RFC Editor status and text for RFCs 1122, 1958, 8200, 9293, 894, and 3234, and the primary ACM end-to-end paper DOI. Current versus historical status and normative versus informational scope remain explicit.

evidence: Checked layer index, SDU, PDU, header, trailer, concatenation, length, efficiency, decoder, header-chain, and round-trip notation for definition before use.
Verified that payload, endpoint, next hop, overhead, and integrity scope always name or imply a declared protocol boundary.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Representation equations are not used as claims about timing, protocol state, trust, or one-to-one packetization.

evidence: Executed the 14, 22, 42, and 60 byte nesting trace and independently recomputed 14/60 = 0.2333.
Recomputed Example 3 as 1,000/1,058 = approximately 94.5 percent.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as 600, 608, 648, and 666 bytes with 600/666 = approximately 90.1 percent.
Recomputed Exercise 3's simplified tunnel limit as 1,500-40 = 1,460 bytes.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All ratios and limits state their exact measurement boundary and excluded overhead; none is presented as observed goodput or universal MTU.

evidence: Re-derived P_i = H_i || S_i || T_i with S_i = P_(i+1), the total-length sum, and boundary efficiency.
Checked decoder and structural round-trip forms against variable-length, normalization, padding, integrity, encryption, and metadata caveats.
Re-derived the forwarding-hop relationship between incoming link decapsulation, permitted network transformation, and outgoing link encapsulation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The equations are obligation decompositions and conditional properties, not a universal semantics for every protocol stack.

evidence: Reviewed truncation, impossible and overflowing lengths, unsupported types, duplicate or reordered options, excessive nesting, decompression expansion, reassembly cost, state timeout, MTU boundaries, filtered errors, and stale path information.
Reviewed NAT, proxy termination, tunneling, fragmentation, offload, encrypted visibility, middlebox state, route change, capture loss, and clock uncertainty.
Reviewed medical telemetry and autonomous rail-control examples for identity, freshness, units, ordering, timing, failover, physical safeguards, and named human authority.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Syntax, integrity, authentication, authorization, resource, operational, and system-safety boundaries remain separate.

evidence: Traced field ownership, complete upper-PDU carriage, demultiplexing, declared/available length agreement, hop scope, defensive rejection, and observation-point invariants through all sections.
Verified the executable model removes prefixes in exact reverse nesting order and limits its claim immediately afterward.
Checked that router, proxy, tunnel endpoint, and application endpoint roles are not conflated.
invariant_checking.notes: No successful lower-layer check or parse is treated as proof of end-to-end delivery, authenticity, authorization, or domain correctness.

evidence: Reviewed the structural round-trip property clause by clause and confirmed its dependence on legal inputs and promised metadata equivalence.
Reviewed the hop-forwarding invariant against mutable IP fields, MTU handling, policy, and error paths.
Reviewed the end-to-end responsibility argument and ensured useful lower-layer mechanisms are not dismissed.
proof_review.notes: The chapter uses bounded design arguments and counterexamples rather than claiming complete protocol or network correctness.

evidence: Audited uses of preserve, complete, exact, valid, safe, integrity, authentic, conformant, proof, and end-to-end.
Confirmed that captures, checksums, decoder success, conformance vectors, tunnels, and encryption are assigned only their actual evidence strength.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: OSI, Internet-suite, vendor, and implementation descriptions remain scoped; no diagram convention is promoted into a universal fact.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/NET-002/report.json records the deterministic prefix-and-strip length trace under the available Python toolchain.
Capture, counter, offload, path-MTU, failover, and consequence-sensitive passages name observation limits and additional evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live-network, performance, interoperability, medical, rail, certification, or external-review claim is made.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed layer, peer protocol, service, implementation interface, SDU, PDU, payload, encapsulation, decapsulation, multiplexing, demultiplexing, endpoint, hop, tunnel, fragmentation, middlebox, and evidence boundary as a coherent model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed real router behavior, proxy termination, variable header chains, tunnel MTU, offload-visible captures, defensive parsing order, resource limits, encrypted inspection, and layer-aware diagnosis. Internal network-practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from three layer relationships through nesting, hop scope, overhead, tunnels, defensive parsing, and evidence. Ten examples and five complete exercises cover classification, tracing, arithmetic, diagnosis, secure design, and high-consequence transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, network-practitioner, standards-body, medical, rail-safety, interoperability, or certification review is claimed.
